one_month_reasoning: No company print in the window: Qualcomm has reported fiscal Q4 exactly 38 days after fiscal year-end three years running (FY23-FY25), and FY26 ended Sep 27, which points to Wed Nov 4, after the Oct 30 window (supervisor finding; I agree). In-window value-chain reads: TSMC mid-October results (N2/N2P ramp that Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 is built on), Samsung prelim and SK hynix/Samsung late-October results (memory pricing; TrendForce sees DRAM +10-15% and NAND +15-20% QoQ in 4Q26, a handset-cost negative that is already known), Apple and MediaTek late-October results, and the first Chinese Snapdragon 8 Elite (Extreme) Gen 6 phone launches after the Sep 22-24 Summit. These are mixed and mostly priced. The stock fell ~9% on Sep 28-29 after a ~35% rally, so reversal and momentum roughly offset. I keep a near-symmetric distribution around $184.5 with monthly sigma ~14% (a little below 54%/3.5 because no earnings print is inside the window), shaded a hair lower to match my slightly-below-spot fair value.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on FY28 (NTM at horizon) non-GAAP EPS ~$11.0 x 16.5x = $181.5 (40%), a sum-of-parts with core EPS ~$9.7 x 14x plus data center ~$1.3/share x 32x = $177.6 (35%), and normalized FCF ~$9.75/share at a 5.5% yield = $177 (25%): ~$179.

inputs_detail.input: Latest quarterly non-GAAP EPS and handset trend

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $10.20 shaded ~2% because industry trackers put the handset downturn into 2027: Counterpoint sees memory prices rallying well through 2027 with normalisation only from late 2027 and 2026 units -14%; IDC -16.7%; TrendForce 4Q26 DRAM +10-15% QoQ; and reports of Exynos 2700 in more S27 models (including some Ultra regions).

FY27 $10.0 plus ~10%: data-center ramp from ~$5B FY27 toward the $15B FY29 target (CFO, Goldman, Sep 8), Gen 6 price increases (>$300/unit vs ~$280) and two-tier flagship mix, auto +double digits, ~2%/yr share shrink; offset by custom-silicon gross-margin drag, Apple product revenue near zero, and a still-weak Android unit base into late 2027.

Stock is ~18x FY27 non-GAAP consensus today with estimates still being cut; handset-era non-GAAP range ~12-17x. I use 16.5x: above the handset-era mid for the growing auto/IoT/data-center mix, but below today's 18x because the Android trough is not yet visible from the value chain and SBC is a large share of non-GAAP EPS.

Between a mature handset-chip yield (~6-7%) and a growth-semis yield (~3-4%), reflecting ~18x non-GAAP P/E today and falling near-term estimates; SBC (~$3.4B/yr) not deducted, which argues against a lower yield.

bear.story: Memory pricing stays elevated through 2027 (Counterpoint: normalisation only from late 2027), Android units keep falling, Samsung puts Exynos 2700 in most S27/S27+ and some Ultra regions, Apple product revenue gone; data center slips below ~$5B in FY27 with few warrant tranches vesting. FY28 EPS ~$9.3 at ~13.5x.

base.story: Handset trough through mid-2027, offset by Gen 6 price increases and the two-tier flagship mix; auto/IoT grow double digits; data center delivers ~$5B in FY27 and ramps toward $8B in FY28; Apple licence secures QTL. FY28 EPS ~$11.2 at ~16.8x.

bull.story: Amazon custom silicon ramps faster with visible warrant vesting, a second hyperscaler win, memory prices plateau so Android flagships recover in 2027; re-rating toward an AI-infrastructure multiple (retest of the $260 high). FY28 EPS ~$12 at ~22x.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$125 (about 12.5x FY27 non-GAAP consensus of $10.2 and at the $121.99 52-week low) the market would be pricing either a failed data-center ramp (Amazon revenue not showing from the December quarter, FY27 well short of ~$5B, no warrant vesting) or a handset share loss beyond Apple (Samsung majority-Exynos including Ultra, Chinese OEMs moving to MediaTek) taking FY27 EPS toward $8.5-9. At 54% vol, $130 sat within ordinary one-sigma noise, so I moved the level down.

reasoning: Round 2 corrects my EPS base: the $9.30 I used was TIKR's undefined 'normalized' NTM figure; company-basis non-GAAP FY27 consensus is ~$10.20 (34 analysts), so QCOM is ~18x, not ~20x, and I re-based both multiples to non-GAAP (P/E 16.5x on FY28, core 14x). I also dropped the 25M warrant share add (treasury-method net ~0.5M; warrant economics go to contra-revenue) and added the 17.8M Modular shares, giving ~1.075B. I re-sourced company figures from the SEC-filed Q3 release rather than StockTitan. Industry follow-ups: Counterpoint now says the memory rally extends through 2027 with normalisation only from late 2027 (2026 units -14%); new reports have Samsung putting Exynos 2700 into some S27 Ultra regions, though other reports say Pro/Ultra keep Snapdragon, so I treat it as a risk, not a number, per the supervisor's note that the Exynos split is a single-broker rumor. Positives: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and a new Extreme tier launched Sep 22-24 on N2P with OEM pricing reported >$300 (vs ~$280), and a Chinese OEM roster (Xiaomi, Oppo, vivo, Honor, OnePlus). Because my value-chain read keeps the Android trough into 2027, I shade FY27 to $10.0 and FY28 to $11.0 (below the supervisor's $11.5). Blended fair value $179 (P/E $181.5, SOTP $177.6, FCF yield $177) vs $182 in round 1, slightly below spot; I centre the 12-month ladder at a median of ~$183 with 80% weight on a 40%-vol lognormal and 20% on a 70%-vol lognormal. Scenario mean 0.27x125 + 0.48x188 + 0.25x265 = $190, consistent with a right-skewed distribution around a ~$183 median. Research in round 2 was 3 searches plus the SEC release; no option data used.
